changes.after: Add the values in an array by visiting each one.

before: foreach (int score in scores) visits each array element in order and gives its current value the local name score for that pass.
An accumulator starts with an initial value, then changes on each visit. total = total + score adds the current element to the running sum.
Changing total does not replace any element of scores. The iteration variable in this ordinary foreach is read-only and cannot be assigned a replacement.
If the array is empty, the body runs zero times. A total initialized to zero therefore stays zero.
Expected behavior from this example: 12. This expected result is a reasoned prediction until a compiler test is recorded.

Optional local transfer task: Try an empty array and a one-element array. Trace the running total after each visit rather than memorizing the final sum. You may trace it on paper if no C# toolchain is installed; reading completion does not certify a run.
after: foreach runs its body once for each value in this array, in order. You do not need to manage an index.
score is the name for the value on the current visit. In this ordinary foreach loop, you cannot assign a replacement to score.
A running total keeps the sum so far. This one starts at zero before the loop begins.
total = total + score adds the current score to the old total and saves the result. It changes total, not the array.
The total goes from 0 to 2, then 6, then 12. The program prints 12 after the loop finishes.
An empty array has no values to visit. The loop body runs zero times, so the starting total stays zero.

0, because there are no visits to change total.

after.question: If scores is empty and total still starts at zero, what prints?
after.explanation: No values are visited, so nothing changes the starting total of zero.
